sections.text: Introduction

This
procedure details the major maintenance Procedure P2 of the circuit breaker should be
carried out every 12 year as indicated by Y12 in the above title block.

This inspection could
be considered as a detailed inspection in addition to routine in inspection
Y6.the inspection items in patrol inspection M1 and routine inspection Y6
should also be done during routine inspection Y12. The stationary arc contact
(2100)should be checked during this inspection . If the wear of the stationary
arc contact (2100) , the moving arc contact (2120)and nozzle (2130) should be
replaced .
Safety Precautions

items:
A work permit
must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety
category,

The circuit
breaker must be isolated completely and grounded on both sides,

Ensure that
the earthing switch must be connected on both sides of the DS.

A work permit
must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable
safety category,

Safety fence
(rope) with caution marks surrounding the work area.

Isolate the DC
voltage. (Switch off the control circuit and Insert closing and tripping
preventive pins.)

Wear safety
helmet, shoes, breathing mask, safety glasses.

Before using a
blower to clean the control cabinet or when cleaning the insulators, wear
breathing mask to protect your lung tissues from the dust particles.

Don't burn the
cloth used in cleaning, collect it and send it to the dump.

sections.text: Inspection and Replacement of Arc Contact and Nozzle

The inspection of the stationary arc contact of the interrupters is performed
according to routine Inspection Y12 sequence shown in Fig .1(b) The inspection
is made with the breaker contact in the open position.

Safety requires the close preventive pin to be instead, DC power disconnected
and air exhausted from the mechanism.

The procedure of the inspection and replacement of 
the arc contacts,
and nozzle of the interrupter is as follows:

items:
Open the inspection cover (2010) by unscrewing the M20x100 bolts as shown
 in fig. 3.

Before starting the inspection work inside the main enclosure (2000) the
 density of the oxygen must be carefully checked. The density of oxygen over
 18 percent in the main enclosure (2000)is definitely required for a safe
 work.

Unscrew the two socket bolts (2276) mounting the stationary contact holder
 (2105) by using the bar spanner (7013) and torque wrench (7020) as shown in
 fig .4. Reach in and take out the stationary contact holder (2105).

Check the wear of the stationary arc contacts (2100). If the wear of the
 parts exceeds the service limits shown in fig. 2 replace with a new one. If the wear of the parts is slight, grind the surfaces of the parts by the
 fine sandpapers and apply very light film of micro-carbon grease, and
 reassemble the above contact in the reversed procedure and skip to 9 (b).

sections.text:
Replacement of the arc contacts and nozzle is as
follows:

Set the inspection bar B(7012) on the moving arc contact
(2120) as shown in fig .6(a), (b).

Unscrew the moving arc contact (2120)by using
the inspection bar B(7012) and torque wrench (7020) and take out the moving arc
contact (2120) by pulling the inspection bar A(7012).

Clean the new stationary arc contact (2100) and new moving arc
contact (2120) using solvent and apply a very light film of micro-carbon grease
to the arc contacts.

items:
Set the inspection bar A(7011)on the nozzle (2130) as shown in
fig .5(a), (b).

Unscrew the nozzle (2130) by using the inspection bar B (7012)
and torque wrench (7020)and take out the nozzle(2130)by pulling the inspection
bar A(7011).

Set the inspection bar B(7012) on the moving arc contact
(2120) as shown in fig .6(a), (b).

Unscrew the moving arc contact (2120)by using
the inspection bar B(7012) and torque wrench (7020) and take out the moving arc
contact (2120) by pulling the inspection bar A(7012).

Clean the new stationary arc contact (2100) and new moving arc
contact (2120) using solvent and apply a very light film of micro-carbon grease
to the arc contacts.

Clean the new nozzle
 (2130) using solvent ethyl alcohol.

Reassemble the above
 contacts and nozzle in the reversed procedure of the above dismounting work
 with special care on the following points:

When mounting the nozzle
 (2130), the nozzle (2130) can be twisted lightly and becomes a little
 heavy to turn. when its twisted further, it becomes light to turn
 again. After it has become light, the nozzle (2130) should be twisted only
 by the inspection bar A (7011) (not by a handle) to the final stop.

Replace the absorbent (zeolite
 F9) (2021).

Renew the O-ring (2500) and the
 gas sealer on the inspection cover (2010).

Clean the inside of the main
 enclosure (2000) carefully.

Close the inspection cover
 (2010) .the lightening torque for the M20 bolts (2015) on the main
 enclosure (2000) is 2,200kg cm.

Evacuate the air in the main
 enclosure (2000). It should be evacuated down to1mmhg. After reaching
 1mmhg, leave the vacuum pump working for at least 30 min. to minimize the
 humidity remaining inside the enclosures.

Fill the enclosures (2000) with
 SF6 gas up to the rated gas pressure.

sections.text: CAUTION:

An enclosure with a high concentration of SF6
 can be hazardous causing asphyxiation from lake of oxygen. before entering
 enclosure, ventilate well and clean interior of powders. A continuous flow of
 dry, fresh air would improve personal conditions and help to keep the
 atmosphere air from entering the enclosure. Refer to the section on SF6 gas
 for precautions in SF6 environment.
Replacement of Absorbent and Rupture Disk
Replacement of absorbent

items:
The absorbent
 assembly (2020) is mounted on the inspection cover (2010) of the main
 enclosure (2000) as shown in Fig .3.The weight of the absorbent (zeolite
 F9)(2021) is approximately 3kg per phase.

The procedure of
 replacement of the absorbent (zeolite F9)(2021) is shown in Fig.3 (refer to
 PI-028).

After renewing the
 absorbent (zeolite F9)(2021), close the inspection cover (2010) within one
 hour and evacuate the air in the enclosure (2000) as soon as possible, as
 the absorbent (zeolite F9) (2021) might absorb too much moisture.

sections.text: Replacement of Rupture Disk (option)

Rupture disk assembly (1030) (Fig. 7), when specified is
provided on the inspection cover (2010). Rupture disk (1031) is to be replaced
every 12 years . Be sure to replace the O-ring (1035) (1036), when the rupture
disk is being replaced.

Replacement of the parts every 6 
years (refer to Fig. 8)

It is recommended to replace the valve seat (3128) and valve
 seal (3318) of the pneumatic operating mechanism every 6 years. The circuit
 breaker should be out of service before coming this work.
Replacement procedure of the parts is as follows:

items: Close the circuit breaker.
Switch off the control circuit.

Exhaust the compressed air in the
 air reservoir (3090) from the drain valve.

Insert the tripping preventing
 pin (3360) (refer to Fig. 8A).

Remove the wiring of the trip
 coil assembly (3380).

Remove the pin (3132) (refer to
 Fig .9(a))

Remove the air piping (3353).
 (Refer to Fig. 9 b).

Remove the bolts A (3398) and
 bolts B(3399) .

Take out the control valve
 assembly (3300).
Replace the valve seat (3128).

Remove the nut (3326) and nylon
 nut (3324) from the driving rod (3352).

Replace the valve seal (3318)
 together with the cylindrical
 valve (3322).

sections.text:
Replacement of the Control Valve Assembly 
 (Refer to Fig. 9)

It is recommended replace the control valve assembly of the
 pneumatic operating mechanism every 5,000 times of operation.

The circuit breaker should be out of service before commencing
 this work.
Replacement Procedure is as follows:

items: Close the circuit breaker.
Switch off the control circuit.

Exhaust the compressed air in the air reservoir (3090)from the drain valve
 .

Insert the tripping preventing pin (3360) (refer to Fig. 
 8A).
Remove the wiring of the trip coil assembly (3380).
Remove the pin (3132) (refer to Fig. 9a)
Remove the air piping (3353). (refer to Fig. 9a).
Remove the bolts A (3398)and bolts B(3399) .
Take out the control valve assembly (3300)
Remove the bolts D (3396) and the trip coil assembly (3380).
Replace the control valve assembly (3300)
